title: Fog, reflection, and directional-light post-processing for a New Zealand landscape (Part 4)

date.basis: Embedded creation time in metadata; transcript references suggest a weather/lighting setup around sunrise.

locations.name: Mount Cook, New Zealand (probable)
locations.basis: Explicit mention of Mount Cook as a framing target and direction in the shot (transcript at ~00:42:58); file path indicates NZ footage.

summary: The video presents a guided, studio‑style walkthrough of a multi-step landscape post‑processing workflow focused on a foggy, sunrise scene captured in New Zealand. It covers fog layering from a prior shot, creating a convincing reflection, color-grading and selective-color corrections for flowers, and a detailed focus-stacking approach. The instructor then digresses into directional-light techniques to sculpt depth, employs Orton-style glow and Vaseline-on-the-lens effects to blend fog with the scene, and emphasizes careful masking, selection, and layer management to preserve foreground subjects while enhancing the overall atmosphere.

sections.title: Fog overlay and sky/foreground integration
sections.description: The narrator explains correcting tilt, notes absence of morning fog, and proposes borrowing fog from a previous shot. They adjust size and color, emphasize that fog can’t move if it intersects foreground elements (e.g., flowers), and begin aligning the fog layer with the current frame.

sections.title: Fog relocation and reflection groundwork
sections.description: Clouds are enlarged and positioned to span the frame; a reflection plan is introduced for the fog layer, including how highlights influence final appearance and separation from the foreground.

sections.title: Color and highlight refinement across the scene
sections.description: The workflow moves through improving peak highlights on the mountains, dialing color toward warm sunrise tones, and applying a multistage color grade. The instructor notes the need to limit blue in the highlights, then explores selective color and magenta/blue interactions to preserve flower hues while warming the sky.

sections.title: Focus stacking workflow and stacking decisions
sections.description: The speaker delves into how many frames to stack, discusses the f/22 halves rule for focus distribution, explains the importance of foreground shots, and demonstrates alignment and blending steps. Emphasis is placed on content-aware fill and saving state before stacking.

sections.title: Directional light, color toning, and edge diffusion
sections.description: A key section on injecting directional light to sculpt three-dimensionality, applying a soft Orton-like glow, and using a Vaseline-on-the-lens analogy. The workflow includes dehazing, selective color/composition refinements, and painting or layering to diffuse edges and maintain focus attention on the light source.

sections.title: Composition-finalization and crop decisions
sections.description: The final steps emphasize cropping to emphasize the strongest angle, ensuring space on the light source side, and referencing the rule of six as a compositional principle. The section closes with remarks on keeping fog cohesive with the background and the importance of layer separation for directional-light edits.
